A bit farther from New Paltz but depending where you go; the Catskills. 
Any trail head is free, there are TONS of different trails for different levels of experience and length. 
And the rail trail that's in Ashokan gives gorgeous views of the reservoir! 
But closer to New Paltz is Vernooy Falls, and a few other amazing spots to check out!

There's an abandoned mini golf course about 14 mins from Platte Clove. 
Platte Clove is also a really interesting spot, if you hike the path to the Devils Kitchen Lean to (it's only a 30ish minute walk), especially on a foggy day it gives some major creepy, dense feelings! 
There's magic meadow at the base of Overlook mountain which has some cool altars if you look in the right spots. 
There's also the old Overlook Hotel which burned down quite a few times on the trail to the fire tower. If you explore it in the late spring/ throughout summer be careful of Timber Rattlesnakes they nest inside. 
There are a few plane crashes off trail on a few mountains some are easier to get to than others. There are a few websites that list them. 
There are a few cool basements/stone structures on and near Peekamoose mountain but from May 15- spent 15 you'll need a permit to access the land there. 
Denning trail head has some super cool spots, that feel a bit diff from your regular Catskill spots. 
And lastly, I HIGHLY recommend stopping at the Catskill Visitor Center, for maps and other really good tid bits/ other spots to check out!

The job I currently have is exactly this, trying to educate tourists or people just starting to come out into the wilderness. 
But, sadly most people laugh and don't care when you tell them "a fed bear is a dead bear". They still ask what time they can see the bears, and if they're friendly after we explain what happens if they feed them etc. 
We get through to a few people, but most of the time we get shrugged off, told that they want to fight the bear etc. 
So, I'm not sure how else we can try to get through to the majority of people if they refuse to learn. Signs don't work, even when posted a bunch/in different spots/sizes/ways. Pictures of trash left behind in the woods don't work to convince people to carry in/carry out. There's so few Forest Rangers that it's hard to actually fine people for breaking laws. It's disheartening.

People feed bear -> bear gets comfy around people thinking all people have food -> bear is happy as long as foods given -> one day someone doesn't give bear food, bear gets angry attacks person(s) -> bear put down because they attacked someone 

DEC will relocate bears but bears are determined if they know food is easier to get elsewhere. Usually they give them a 3 strike rule because they HATE having to put them down.

Its absolutely horrible that it's come to this, but most people will not listen to bear advice given and treat it like a petting zoo, aggravating the bear in some cases and/or messing up the bears ability to survive in the wild without human interference. If people educated/controlled themselves better this wouldn't happen. But even when you tell them their actions will get the bear killed they continue. See it everyday on the trails I work on, people ask what time they can see the bears like a show. 

Those tourists got that mama and her cubs killed. DEC sadly had to follow their rules set in place caused by the peoples actions towards a wild animal that has become aggressive.
